answers.problem: An astronaut walking on Mars, with no GPS, has to know whether she can still get back to the habitat on her oxygen. The example puts her 913 m out at Cheyava Falls with a dust storm coming. The walk home costs 18 min and 54 g of O2 on the real slopes, and NASA rules cap the EVA at 8 h, keep a 30 min O2 reserve untouched and forbid slopes over 20 degrees.
answers.what_it_does: It is a browser app with two modes. At a table the crew plans a route from their goal, crew size, time, O2 and battery, and the route goes around no-go slopes on a HiRISE slope map. In a first-person helmet view they walk the route with a visor HUD showing margin, route, position from terrain matching, a minimap, a sampling checklist and weather. A dust storm or radiation alert re-plans the route home (a shelter detour, for example). Afterwards a review screen compares the walked track to the plan and charts margin over the reserve. The core idea is one visor number, the margin, which equals what is left after O2 used, the priced walk home (+20 percent, Apollo 15 rule) and a 30 min reserve (Apollo 17), recomputed every metre.
answers.nasa_data: MRO HiRISE 1 m terrain model (JEZ_hirise_soc_006) and its 25 cm image give slope, route, walking cost, radio shadow and position fixes. Perseverance Mastcam-Z images and traverse (sols 1140 to 1266) give science stops, Cheyava Falls photos and the rover's drives. Perseverance MEDA sol 1187 gives temperature, wind and dust for the conditions outlook. Curiosity RAD data from the September 2017 event (date from NASA DONKI) drives the radiation alert and visor dose. NASA suit and walkback tests (NASA/TP-2009-214796, Apollo 15 and 17 rules, xEVA ConOps) give O2 per metre, the 30 min reserve, the 20 degree limit and the 8 h EVA.
answers.real_vs_simulated: Each on-screen number carries a tag. DATA means measured by a mission or set in a NASA document, such as terrain height, RAD dose rates and the 20 degree limit. DERIVED means the team calculated it from DATA, such as slope, O2 left and distance walked. SIM means a team assumption, such as the 1 m/s walking speed and the storm's arrival time. The terrain matches NASA Mars Trek's HiRISE model to 0.14 m RMS over 564,001 points. Radiation was measured in Gale crater, not Jezero, and the screen says so. On the visor, range, bearing, the nav fix and the margin itself are tagged SIM.
answers.who_made_it: Team Los Frijolitos Espaciales Refritos Nueva Generación from Ensenada, Mexico: Fernando Haro, Antonio Ramos González, Jorge Vázquez, Andrea Rivas Gómez, Brayan Iván Pérez and Teresa Rivas. Challenge is NASA Space Apps 2026, Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.
answers.margin: +480 min on the idea slide's visor, labelled 'MARGIN NOW, home in 0 min' and tagged SIM. The React screenshot shows +399 min, and the review chart's lowest point is 229 min at T+0:02:43.

looked_at: Slide 1 gave the name, thesis, team, location and challenge. Slide 2 gave the problem and the NASA limits. Slide 3 gave the margin concept and the +480 visor number. Slide 4 gave the plan, walk, react and review flow. Slide 5 gave the NASA datasets and what each one feeds. Slide 6 gave the DATA, DERIVED and SIM tags and the 0.14 m validation. Slide 7 gave users, next steps and the URL.
confused_by: Margin is in minutes, but slide 3 frames it as O2 'you can still spend' and slide 2 prices the walk in grams, so I had to infer that O2 converts to time. +480 min equals the 8 h EVA cap, so I could not tell whether O2 or the clock limits it. The margin is tagged SIM even though slide 3 says it is recomputed from HiRISE and suit tests, which sounds DERIVED. Three margin values (+480, +399, 229) appear and none is called the demo's key number. Jezero is never named as the site until slide 6 mentions it in passing. 'She' on slide 2 is never introduced. '8 h · 30 min · 20°' is dense to decode. On slide 1 the challenge title overlaps the HUD compass and faint ghost panels sit behind the title, and the footer about the margin on the visor is too small to read. 'Our terrain' on slide 6 does not say what was built if HiRISE is the source.
faster_if: Name the site (Jezero crater, Cheyava Falls) and the user (an astronaut on EVA) on slide 1 or 2. Say on slide 3 that margin is minutes of O2 left after the walk home and reserve, and use one margin value across the deck with a callout on the visor screenshot. Explain why margin is SIM, or retag it DERIVED. Label the three numbers on slide 2 instead of joining them with dots. Put the challenge name on its own line, clear of the HUD.
